title: Event cards that fit any screen

terminal.description: The page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. Make the panel narrow and wide to see the page as a phone and a desktop would. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Swap the floats for flex rows
tasks.description:
Lay out the two rows on the page with flexbox instead of floats.

The check looks at the page's `<header>` and at each card's `.event-footer`. For both it wants:

- `display: flex` at every width
- the items spread to the two ends of the row: `justify-content` is `space-between`, `space-around` or `space-evenly`, or one item has an `auto` left margin
- `flex-wrap: wrap`, so items can move to a new line on a phone

It also checks that no `float: left` or `float: right` is left in `styles.css`.
nextSteps: Find every `float` in `styles.css` and the `overflow: hidden` rules that were there to hold them.
Make the header a flex container and spread its two groups apart.
Make the Browser panel narrow, check that the rows wrap instead of overlapping, then press Check.
hints: Flex works on the children of the element you set it on. Set it on the row, not on the items.
Free space in a flex row goes where `justify-content` says. Space between the items pushes the first and last to the ends.
Each row needs three declarations: `display`, `justify-content` and `flex-wrap`. `align-items: center` and a `gap` make it look tidy too.

tasks.title: One column on a phone, several on a wide screen
tasks.description:
Lay out the event list as a grid that adapts to the screen.

The check looks for:

- a `<meta name="viewport">` in the head whose content includes `width=device-width`
- `.event-list` is a grid with at least two columns at 1280px wide
- one column at 375px wide (a grid with one column, or no grid at all)
- the list items and the `.event` cards no longer set a `width` (other than `auto` or `100%`)

Either a `grid-template-columns` that fills the row with columns of a smallest size, or a media query that changes the columns, is fine. The check assumes the list has about 912px of room at 1280px wide and 327px at 375px wide.
nextSteps: Add the viewport meta tag to the head of `index.html`.
Remove the `display: inline-block` and `width` rule that put the cards side by side.
Make `.event-list` a grid with a gap.
Choose its columns so a phone gets one and a wide screen gets several, then press Check.
hints: Percent widths shrink with the screen, so three cards stay side by side on a phone and get squashed. A grid can change the number of columns instead.
`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(...))` makes as many columns as fit, each at least a given size.
Pick a smallest column size that fits once in 327px but at least twice in 912px, such as somewhere between 14rem and 20rem.

tasks.title: Keep pictures and long words inside the card
tasks.description:
Stop the pictures and the long hashtag from poking out of narrow cards.

The check looks for:

- every picture in an `.event` card has `max-width: 100%` (or `width: 100%`), and its height is `auto` or not set, unless you set `object-fit` or `aspect-ratio`
- the paragraph with `#QuillmoorWinterReadingChallenge`, or an element around it, has `overflow-wrap` (or `word-break`) set to a value that lets a long word break
nextSteps: Make the Browser panel narrow and find what sticks out of the cards.
Replace the fixed picture width with a limit of the card's width.
Let the height follow the width so the picture keeps its shape.
Let long words break inside the cards, then press Check.
hints: A fixed width in pixels does not care how wide its box is. A limit in percent does.
When you set only the width of an image, the browser works out the height from its shape. A fixed height stretches it.
`overflow-wrap` decides what happens to a word too long for its line. It is inherited, so setting it on the card covers every paragraph in it.
